bbc.label: BBC One, 31 Aug 1997: the news interrupts a film (BBC bulletin via archive.org)
subs: This is BBC One. We have interrupted our programs for a news report. We now go over to Martin Lewis in the news studio.
We interrupt this film to tell you we are getting reports that Diana, Princess of Wales,
has been badly injured in a car crash in France.
French radio is saying that the accident happened in Western Paris when the car she was travelling
in collided with another vehicle in a tunnel.

ap.label: NBC News, 30 Aug 1997 (US evening): wire bulletin read on air
subs: The latest associated press bulletin is one eerie line.
It just says simply reading off the live wire copy here.
She was 36.

blair.label: ITN News, 31 Aug 1997: Prime Minister Tony Blair
subs: people. She was the people's princess and that's how she will stay, how she will remain in our hearts

spencer.label: ITN News, 31 Aug 1997: Earl Spencer's statement
subs: However, I would say that I always believed the press would kill her in the end.
But not even I could imagine that they would take such a direct hand in her death, as seems to be the case.
It would appear that every proprietor and editor of every publication that has paid for intrusive and exploitative photographs of her,
encouraging greedy and ruthless individuals to risk everything in pursuit of Diana's image, has blood on his hands today.

owen.label: ITN News, 31 Aug 1997: Nicholas Owen at Kensington Gardens
subs: And you know the odd thing to me really is how quiet it really is here.
Yes, there's the noise of traffic, London traffic going on as ever behind us.
But in this park, you know, there's a little bit of hubbub but not much.
It's really very, very quiet indeed.

q_a.label: The Queen's broadcast, 5 Sep 1997 (AAPB / PBS NewsHour archive)
subs: First, I want to pay tribute to Diana myself.
She was an exceptional and gifted human being.
In good times and bad, she never lost her capacity
to smile and laugh, nor to inspire others
with her warmth and kindness.

q_b.label: The Queen's broadcast, 5 Sep 1997 (AAPB / PBS NewsHour archive)
subs: This is also an opportunity for me on behalf of my family
and especially Prince Charles and William and Harry
to thank all of you who have brought flowers,
sent messages, and paid your respects in so many ways
to a remarkable person.

q_c.label: The Queen's broadcast, 5 Sep 1997 (AAPB / PBS NewsHour archive)
subs: I hope that tomorrow we can all, wherever we are,
join in expressing our grief at Diana's loss
and gratitude for her all too short life.
It is a chance to show to the whole world
the British nation united in grief and respect.
May those who died rest in peace.
And may we, each and every one of us,
Thank God for someone who made many, many people happy.

sil.label: ITV funeral coverage, 6 Sep 1997: the route, in silence
subs: eyes fixed on the gates and silence will mark this procession,
no military bands, no music, no shouts of command, silence,

eul.label: CBS News funeral coverage, 6 Sep 1997: Earl Spencer's eulogy
subs: to those at the opposite end of the moral spectrum. It is a point to remember that of
all the ironies about Diana, perhaps the greatest was this. A girl given the name of the ancient
goddess of hunting was, in the end, the most hunted person of the modern age. She would
She wants us today to pledge ourselves to protecting her beloved boys William and Harry
from a similar fate, and I do this here, Diana, on your behalf.

clin.label: CBS News, 6 Sep 1997: statement from Hillary Clinton read on air
subs: Mark Phillips, thanks. The first lady of the United States, Hillary Rodham Clinton, issued
a statement at Winfield House, the residents of the American Ambassador Hill, and it says
in part on behalf of the president and the American people, I came here to express our
deep sadness at the loss of Diana. She did hard work in difficult places and she softened
arts and lifted spirits. We can honor Diana's memory by continuing her work.
